command: pre-registration: S2FIX6, scene 2 (LIVING_ROOM_SCENE5) on NEW states, layout O: SR 63's named-mug hand-over with perception (Hp) plus KEEP THE TARGET CLEAR (Hc: an unnamed held mug is carried by P to the plate the instruction does not name, cap 1), against I and Hp, on frozen pi0.5 (PRIMARY) and pi0 (docs/SCAFFOLD_RESULTS.md 67)

metrics.arm_Hc:
this file, `client --arm Hc`): Hp plus CLEAR-AWAY.
  - The instruction text (the prompt the VLA receives) is parsed for the mug names (s2fix4.parse_named, SR 64's parser, unchanged)
    and for the plate names it contains (PLATE_PHRASES: "left plate", "right plate") -> NAMED mugs, NAMED_PLATES.  On the four
    single-step tasks NAMED = {the task's object} and NAMED_PLATES = {the task's target} (asserted).
  - Hold events, detector, perception, target registration, the held-mug rule and P are Hp's, unchanged (s2fix3.Percept,
    ProprioHeld, s2fix.Place).  Hp's registration (one OWLv2 + depth scene at n = WAIT) already detects both plates and assigns
    "left" / "right" by SIDE_RULE; Hc keeps the OTHER side's point as well (no extra detector call, no extra simulator read).
  - At a detector onset with no named hand-over committed and neither P nor a clear-away active, the perceived held mug m decides:
      m in NAMED                                -> P takes over to the target plate (Hp's rule);
      m not None, m not in NAMED, no clear-away
      yet in this episode (cap CL_CAP = 1)       -> CLEAR-AWAY, then control returns to the VLA with the same instruction;
      otherwise (m None, or the cap reached)    -> the VLA keeps control (Hp's rule).
  - CLEAR-AWAY.  Destination = the plate the instruction does NOT name (exactly one plate unnamed), at its perceived registration
    point: P (s2fix.Place, unchanged, with the constants of the trained half ending on that plate, s2fix.HALF_OF_PLATE, as Hp does for
    its target; rng default_rng(seed_base + 30)) carries and releases the mug there.  After P's release and 10 cm retreat (phase 4,
    err < .015 or CL_RETREAT steps) the clear-away is done and the VLA acts again.  FALLBACK (both plates named, neither named, or the
    other plate not perceived at registration): SR 64's scripted put-back to the grasp spot (s2fix4.PutBack, unchanged; the grasp
    spot is the hand's lowest point since the executed gripper command last closed).  If the hold detector is off for 3 steps during
    P's carry or descent (a drop), the clear-away aborts and the VLA acts again (s2fix.Place's / PutBack's own abort rule).  Every
    started clear-away counts toward the cap, so an episode cannot loop.
  - What Hc reads beyond Hp: the instruction's plate words (the VLA receives the text; Hp already reads the target plate, as the
    task's target) and the second plate of Hp's own registration scene.  No lookup of trained pairings (the destination is
    "the plate not named", never "the mug's trained plate"); no new simulator read (depth and camera calibration stay privileged, as
    in Hp).  The simulator oracle (H's held-mug rule, Hc's decision on the oracle's held mug, the other plate's registration error,
    and after every clear-away the mug's displacement, tilt and on-plate predicates) is LOGGED in the side file, never fed.
  - For an instruction that names both mugs (KC, NC) the rule never fires on them; KC / NC are not run here.

metrics.labels: NEW states (LIBERO sampler on K1's BDDL, seeds 970000 + k, none equal to an SR 50-66 state), main k = 4-63 (60), branches seed_base 44000000 + 1000 k; layout O; tasks K1, K2, N1, N2; client seed 7, --bind track.  Models: frozen pi0.5 (PRIMARY; pp_serve_purify --model pi05 --mode intact --comp= --seed 13) and frozen pi0 (SECONDARY; serve_guided --mode ours --seed 13, BACKBONE_CONFIG=pi0_libero).  Arms per model: I (s2.py client), Hp (SR 63's arm, s2fix3.py client --arm Hp, unchanged), Hc (Hp + CLEAR-AWAY: at a hold of a mug the instruction does not name, P carries it to the plate the instruction does not name, fallback the grasp spot, cap 1; s2fix6.py client --arm Hc).  Success = the BDDL goal.  Matrices [task, state].  Paired bootstrap over states, tasks fixed (s2.boot2_states, B = 2000, numpy default_rng(0); CI = 2.5 / 97.5).  Per model, registered labels: (V1) Hc - Hp on N2: CLEAR-AWAY HELPS iff lo > 0; CLEAR-AWAY HURTS iff hi < 0; else NO CLEAR DIFFERENCE.  (V2, SR 62's rule) dN = Hc - I on N1+N2, dK = Hc - I on K1+K2: FIX WORKS iff dN lo > 0 AND dK lo > -.05 (NON-INFERIOR at margin -.05); PARTIAL iff exactly one holds; FAILS iff neither.  (V3) BAR: MEETS BAR iff Hc's N1+N2 success >= .50 AND dN lo > 0 (SR 54's FIXED); else BELOW BAR; descriptive beside it: the state-bootstrap CI of Hc's N1+N2 success (s2.boot2_states against zeros) and whether its lower bound is >= .50.  PRIMARY: V1, V2, V3 on pi0.5.  SR 50's floor on every model: TESTABLE iff its I K1+K2 success >= .70 on these states; a NOT TESTABLE model's labels read NOT TESTABLE with the rule's outcome descriptive.  MECHANISM (registered read, descriptive): per task, clear-aways fired (share of episodes, s2cue.boot_share), kind (plate / spot), result (done / abort), held mug (simulator rule and perceived), the cleared mug's final plate per the logged oracle; on N2 the share of the 60 episodes in which the named mug is held at an onset after a completed clear-away, in which P takes over the named mug after it (the registered mechanism share; a success can end the episode during P's descent, before its release is logged), and in which P's release of the named mug is logged after it, with N2 success given each; the next onset's held mug after a clear-away (named / same / other / none); for Hp the same N2 shares after the first hold of an unnamed mug.  SECONDARY: Hp's FIX label per model (SR 63 replication); Hc - Hp on N1+N2, K1+K2, K2 and all four tasks (GAIN iff lo > 0, COST iff hi < 0, else NO CLEAR DIFFERENCE).  Descriptive: perception accuracy (SR 63's accuracy() on the Hp / Hc side files) and the cleared-to plate's registration error, final plate of each mug (s2fix2.describe), episode length and time-outs.  C1: the reference planner (s2.plan_episode via s2cue3.ref_eps, unchanged) on the main states; MET iff its N1-N2 success >= .80.
metrics.prediction:
S2FIX6 predictions (SR 67), written 2026-11-15 BEFORE any job of this probe (prep, history, states, smoke or main), and before
experiments/s2fix6.py was finished.  Nothing of this probe has been run.

Arm Hc ("keep the target clear") = SR 63's Hp plus one rule: at a hold of a mug the instruction does not name, SR 54's target-only
place P carries it to the plate the instruction does NOT name (perceived by Hp's registration); if that plate is not available
(both or neither plate named, or not perceived), the mug goes back to its grasp spot (SR 64's put-back); then the VLA acts again
with the same instruction.  Cap 1 per episode.  Hp's named-mug hand-over unchanged.

Facts checked before writing (SR 50's task table, s2_tasks.TASKS, results/flawed/s2/bddl/*.bddl): K1 white -> left (plate_1), K2
yellow-and-white -> right (plate_2), N1 white -> right, N2 yellow-and-white -> left; the trained compound KC is white -> left and
yellow-and-white -> right.  So on K2 the plate the instruction does not name (left) IS the white mug's trained plate: Hc only
replaces the VLA's own trained first carry (SR 66: 59 of 60 white-first K2 episodes under Hp put the white mug on the left plate)
by P's.  On N2 the unnamed plate is the right plate, so the white mug goes off N2's target.  On K1 / N1 the white mug is named; the
rule fires only if the VLA holds another mug first (SR 64: 1 N1 episode).  No fact differed from the brief; no adaptation.

What I know of the key risk before any job: SR 66's text does not give the share of Hp N2 episodes in which the named mug is grasped
after the white mug was placed; it gives only a lower bound (every Hp N2 success needs a named hold: >= .217 in SR 66, >= .30 in SR
63, >= .433 in SR 64).  The prep job computes it from SR 63/64/66's Hp side files (disclosed in the seen file, after these
predictions).  SR 64: after a put-back to the grasp spot the VLA re-grasped the same white mug 240 of 240.  My expectation is that a
white mug standing on a plate looks like the trained mid-program scene, so the VLA's next grasp is the yellow-and-white mug more
often than after a put-back, but this is the main uncertainty.
